doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: Cleaning up Bourbon Street and the Super Bowl
summary: Pete and Ramsey discuss litter cleanup on Bourbon Street and how New Orleans won the Super Bowl effort.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Bye. 522-3791 is the number. We have five lines open. Pete, are you satisfied with the way the drive to clean up Bourbon Street of litter and corn cobs and like that turned out? Oh, yeah.

You know, we had a couple of the places that just moved back a few feet, like not any smallest restaurants in the world. But we don't see as much of the corn cobs or the stuff on the street. I know. I think it looks a lot cleaner. The street looks a lot cleaner than me. Doesn't it? Do you, Pete? I think they're going to have to if they want to keep the conventions down here or the Super Bowl again. That would be great if we could get the Super Bowl every year. Well, the way... That would be fantastic.
Roselle said today that he was very pleased with the way New Orleans has handled it and that we'll be in strong consideration for next year. I think it's going to be tough for Miami to get it back.
I think so, too. I think the governor of Florida made a statement, too, that he said that they already missed the boat. The Floridians missed the boat.

Well, yesterday, the governor blamed it on the Dade County officials, and today the Dade County officials blamed it on the governor. So here maybe we're able to work together. Sounds like our politicians. Yeah. You know, frankly, a lot of people were surprised that our politicians and civic leaders were able to get together and grab this thing. They may be a good sign.
I think Skiro went up there and, you know, he really fought for this. And George Healy, of course. Right.
A big factor. Hello. Go ahead. All right. Hello. Go ahead.
